title: Later Jin Dynasty
capsule: The Later Jin (後金) was a Jurchen-Manchu state established in 1616 by Nurhaci, who unified the Jurchen tribes and proclaimed himself Khan of the Later Jin in Hetu Ala, drawing a deliberate parallel with the earlier Jin dynasty (1115–1234). After Nurhaci's death in 1626, his son Hong Taiji reorganized the administration, adopted the Chinese imperial model, created the Eight Banners system, and renamed the state 'Qing' (清) and the people 'Manchu' in 1635–1636. The state then invaded Ming China, and the Shunzhi Emperor entered Beijing on 6 June 1644 following the fall of the Ming; the dataset's terminal date of 1645 reflects the early Qing consolidation of the North China Plain rather than full conquest.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Jurchen homeland and Liaodong territories are well documented in both Chinese and Manchu sources; the exact boundaries of control in the steppe frontier zones are approximately reconstructed.
